In thunderbird, there is no email database. Each message folder retains all messages. If your accounts are POP, an easy way to save them is to do this:

  1. install the importexporttools NG addon
  2. highlight a folder to be saved, rightclick, and select importexport option to export as mbox file
  3. next, highlight Local Folders, rightclick and select importexport option to import mbox
  4. repeat the prior 2 steps for each desired folder
  5. check that the copied folders are all correct
  6. you have now saved all the messages to Local Folders and the POP account may be removed.

content: You messed up your profile migration since you transferred only your profile folder and not the entire folder Thunderbird from your old Mac. This is one of the most frequent errors when migrating to a new computer. If you still have access to your old Mac copy the entire "Thunderbird" folder from your user library and transfer it on Desktop of the new Mac. On the new Mac verify that Thunderbird in not running, open your user library, rename the folder Thunderbird in Thunderbird-old and move it on your Desktop. Move the Thunderbird folder you just imported from old Mac in your user library and start Thunderbird.

content:
thomasjp said
When I copied and pasted the profile from mac #1 into the Thunderbird/profiles files in mac #2 then launched TB I get a message Profile Missing: Your Thunderbird profile cannot be loaded . it may be missing or inaccessible.

Just a short explanation for the failure of your profile migration: when you launched TB the first time on the new Mac it created a folder Thunderbird in your user Library. This folder Thunderbird contained a folder Profiles and within it a virgin profile folder somewhat like "1234abcd.default-release". At the same time a text file profiles.ini was created in the Thunderbird folder. It contains the path to the profile folder 1234abcd.default-release: each time you start Thunderbird it first reads the profiles.ini file to know which profile folder to use (to open). Obviously you replaced the new virgin profile folder 1234abcd.default-release with the 7n1rgaj8f.default profile folder you had copied from the old Mac. But when you restarted TB it read the profiles.ini file, looked for the virgin 1234abcd.default-release profile folder and could not find it since now there was a folder with another name. This explains the message "Your Thunderbird profile cannot be loaded".

I have to admit that the Help article you linked can be misinterpreted, in particular the point "From your Thunderbird profile folder in Finder, open the Go menu and select Enclosing Folder two times."

that is good - leave it selected.

But if by accident you have set up emails to be ignored, then the count will not change but the ignored emails will not display even if 'All' is selected. 'All' does not include anything you set up as ignored. You need to check, so select 'View' > 'Threads' > 'Ignored Threads' Do more emails now display ?

If yes, then you need to remove the 'ignore thread' setting: Right click on email and you will see the 'Ignored thread' selected - click on it to remove the ignore setting.
